result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with multi-story commercial and residential buildings. While sidewalks are present on both sides, there is a lack of marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals at the immediate intersection, forcing pedestrians to cross unmarked pavement.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: A pedestrian is shown crossing the street where there are no painted markings or signage to alert drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, left side crossing to the right

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The roadway surface is uneven with visible patching and cracking, which can be a trip hazard.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings to clearly define the pedestrian path and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corner to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: ADA Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile warning strips and sloped ramps to ensure the crossing is accessible for all users.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with marked crosswalks and wide sidewalks in a commercial/mixed-use area. While basic infrastructure like traffic signals and street lighting is present, the crossing distance is moderate and there is no physical separation like a refuge island.

hazards.name: Lack of physical protection
hazards.description: Pedestrians crossing the street have no physical protection or refuge mid-way, increasing exposure to traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with wide sidewalks and marked crosswalks, though the markings are significantly faded. Pedestrians are visible crossing the street, and traffic signals are present to manage vehicle and pedestrian flow.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The continental-style crosswalk markings are heavily worn and faded, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center right, across the side street

hazards.name: Poor Roadway Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and uneven asphalt in the intersection area could present a trip hazard or affect vehicle braking.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Refresh
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalks with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver awareness of the crossing zone.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulbout)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a dense urban commercial environment with wide sidewalks and a marked high-visibility crosswalk. While pedestrian signals and traffic lights are present, the crossing distance across multiple lanes and the presence of outdoor dining furniture near the walkway require careful navigation.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple travel lanes and a parking lane without a median or refuge island.

hazards.name: Potential Sidewalk Encroachment
hazards.description: Outdoor dining furniture and signage on the right side narrow the effective walking width of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side sidewalk near the restaurant
